rv.q: It's easily the funniest thing to arrive on Broadway since 'The Book of Mormon.'
Certainly the most fun of the spring musical openings on Broadway, "Something Rotten!" is a sharply directed piece that achieves a consistent world and never checks its own literacy.
Although comic desperation descends on the second act, it’s still a deliriously funny show.
Nicholaw’s genius for reducing an audience to helpless giggles is on blazing display in Something Rotten!
Even if the show doesn’t finish as strongly as it starts, its giddy high spirits prevail.
Something Rotten! makes for a decidedly better night at the theater than many other shows that have benefited from a test run.
This cheerfully anachronistic musical comedy about the invention of the musical comedy is a kaleidoscope of inside jokes, self-referential gags and winking tributes to the theater.
The show is exuberantly silly, and if you're in the mood for that brand of theatrical comfort food — a helping of song, dance and snark — 'Something Rotten!' delivers.
Even if you haven't brushed up on your Shakespeare recently — or your musical theater — you'll find plenty that's amusing, if little that's memorable, in Something Rotten!
It's a show that knows exactly what it is: a big, goofy, self-aware piece of musical-theater fan service.
The show's good-natured silly charms just feel hammered by an unrelenting tsunami of manic, frenetic, zanier-than-zaniest onslaught of collegiate show-biz humor.
Nevertheless, this one’s for backward sophomores only.

It’s softly vulgar – there’s a near rhyme of “penis” and “genius”, to say nothing of those gluteal gyrations – but it settles for sweet when it ought to be scurrilous, comfortable when it ought to be really clever.
It is, quite simply, the best musical I have seen in ages, and producer Kevin McCollum has a hit on his hands.
"Something Rotten” is red meat for theatre lovers – it’s clever, bodaciously funny, ridiculously tuneful; and even if Act II feels a bit overdone, audiences are sure to eat it up.

"The new musical 'Something Rotten!' offers something rare, as well as something recycled. The something rare is the opportunity for no fewer than three leading men to astonish us in entirely different ways...“Something Rotten!” turns into something recycled.
A high-spirited, gleefully acted, past-meets-present cultural mash-up, mixing high wit with low jokes.
What carries you through is the evident fun being had by the cast
Even if you don’t get every allusion, the staging by choreographer and director Casey Nicholaw (“The Book of Mormon” and “Aladdin”) is consistently fun.
With great comedic timing and expression, James is perfectly cast as the striver Nick.
Even so, “Something Rotten!” is a great deal of cartoonish fun, especially for musical theater fans who can appreciate the inside references, which range from the megahit “Cats” to the flop “Chess.”
It will be a winner with all who enjoy new-fangled takes on old-fashioned musical parodies.

Something Rotten! revels in its silliness while delivering such a nonstop blitzkrieg of production numbers, each out-doing the one before, that you hardly notice how much you've fallen in love with the Bottom bros...

"“Rotten!” paints musical theater culture in the same broad strokes that the “The Book of Mormon” used to satirize religion—everyone gets to be in on the joke. This new musical makes us do just enough work that we feel satisfied for picking up on them.
Something Rotten! is a very funny show indeed, and should please audiences although one wonders how non-theatre savvy houses will respond to all those musical comedy jokes.
By the time this initially delightful, eventually repetitive Broadway extravaganza ends, you too may feel a slight impatience not only with Shakespeare but with the entire musical theatre genre.
'Something Rotten!' has established itself as Broadway's funniest, splashiest, slap-happiest musical comedy in at least 400 years.
I haven't had such a good, silly time at the theater since 'Spamalot' or maybe 'The Producers'
SOMETHING ROTTEN! contains more laughs than all our other current Broadway shows combined.
This show is a riot and MUST SEE for musical theater fans

A rare theatrical event…a wonderful musical farce. Anyone who wants to go to the theatre and have a great time, unburdened by a complicated plot, listen to fun lyrics, and experience two acts of non-stop laughter…this “very new musical” should be their play of choice!
It's a blissfully entertaining show that doesn't pretend to contain anything particularly original.
But it’s the writers, all making their Broadway debuts, who emerge as the biggest stars, imbuing Something Rotten! with smart-alecky glee.

"Seldom does the Great White Way see a sillier version of the highbrow and a smarter version of the lowbrow in one show. The laugh-a-minute book by Kirkpatrick and O’Farrell, observes all the conventional structure of the musical comedy genre, but transports it to a level of unadulterated fun not achieved often enough...
Something Rotten!, a boisterous and jaunty ride not to be missed.
Something Rotten! is that rare piece of fluff that knows exactly where it stands while occasionally betraying an unexpected intelligence.

Riddled throughout with stage-related gags – suggesting “Forbidden Broadway” on psychedelics -- the madcap “Something Rotten!” obviously represents far too much of a good thing, but it undeniably gets mighty hilarious at times.
Though often grossly (and unabashedly) overplayed, overall the show's on-the-nose wit is disarmingly funny and likely to charm.
Casey Nicholaw pulls out every trick in the theatrical book to keep you from laughing so hard and smiling so much
If you like Spamalot you're going to like this show.
Jam-packed with all the ingredients of a surefire smash hit, Something Rotten is funny without being unnecessarily smutty
Rotten this show is anything but.
By the end of the show, despite the cleverness of its concept, Something Rotten as executed simply hasn't added up to a completely satisfying musical.
